newsitem.title: UK: Matthew Clark xmas trade shadows industry.
newsitem.headline: Matthew Clark xmas trade shadows industry.

text.p: Troubled cider-maker Matthew Clark, whose shares lost half their value last September when it warned its sales were under fire from the rising popularity of "alcopops", said on Tuesday that its Christmas trading was in line with the industry and slightly below expectations.
The company also said it expects to maintain its total dividend payment for the year and unveiled a big advertising campaign aimed at rejuvinating its major brands -- Diamond White and Blackthorn.
Matthew Clark holiday trade in line with =2
"The board is confident that the innovative new cider marketing strategies will achieve a rejuvenation of the group's major cider brands," said chief executive Peter Aikens.
Competition from alcopops -- cola and fruit flavoured alcoholic drinks -- hit sales of Matthew Clark's Diamond White and K, stripping about 11.0 million off annual profits.

Price competition also led to lower margins for the company, taking an estimated 4.0 million off annual profits. Tougher rivalry among cider makers for contracts with national and regional brewers stripped some 7.0 million from annual profits.
The company acknowledged the management put in place after it acquired Taunton Cider did not work effectively and customers suffered from disruption until May 1996.

To turn the company around Matthew Clark plans to develop its brands. Blackthorn cider will be relaunched in the spring through a TV-led advertising campaign and a new product -- Blackthorn Gold -- will be launched.
The company will spend about 52 million pounds on marketing in the financial year to April 30, 1998, which includes much higher advertising expenditure of between 8.0 and 10.0 million.

Price rises of Matthew Clark brands will also take effect from this month. The company reported pre-tax profits of 21.6 million pounds for the six months to October 31, up 40 percent but well below its own expectations.
